title: 'Women Demand Life' Protesters Rally in Tel Aviv for October 7 Commission of Inquiry
detail: The Women Demand Life movement held a demonstration in Tel Aviv on Sunday morning, August 9, 2026, calling for a state commission of inquiry into the security and government failures of October 7. The gathering honored the six hostages murdered by Hamas captors in August 2024 — Hersh Goldberg-Polin, Eden Yerushalmi, Carmel Gat, Almog Sarusi, Alexander Lobanov, and Ori Danino — two days after Goldberg-Polin's second yahrzeit was marked in Jerusalem. Demonstrators held cutouts of the hostages' faces and a large banner reading 'We won't forget, they could have returned alive.' The protest is the latest in a sustained series of accountability actions by bereaved and hostage families as the government continues to resist establishing a state commission ahead of the October 27, 2026 election.

media.caption: Women Demand Life protesters hold cutouts of hostages murdered by Hamas, demanding a state commission of inquiry

title: IDF and Shin Bet Publicly Acknowledge 'Nili' Unit's Campaign to Hunt Down Every October 7 Perpetrator
detail: The IDF and Shin Bet, in a first-of-its-kind report by Channel 12 published August 9, 2026, publicly acknowledged a joint special unit codenamed 'Nili' (after the World War I-era Jewish underground intelligence network Netzach Yisrael Lo Yishaker) that has spent nearly three years compiling and working through a list of roughly 5,000 people involved in the October 7, 2023 attack, hostage-taking, and captive abuse. Officers described using facial recognition software, AI-assisted analysis of video the attackers filmed of themselves, detainee interrogations, and human intelligence to identify targets ranging from low-level participants to senior Hamas commanders, then tracking their daily routines to plan precision strikes. Roughly 2,800 people on the list have been killed and the unit says it will continue 'until the last' name is found. The disclosure came as the manhunt was reported to have paused at the start of August after the US-led Board of Peace's Gaza roadmap called for a halt to Israeli strikes — even though Prime Minister Netanyahu publicly rejected the roadmap and IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir vowed the military would keep 'operating proactively' against Hamas.

media.caption: Gazans breach the Israel-Gaza border fence on October 7, 2023 — file photo used to illustrate reporting on the 'Nili' unit's manhunt for the attack's perpetrators
